newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH rises on meeting with British firms.
newsitem.headline: LVMH rises on meeting with British firms.

text.p: Shares in LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton rose against the trend on Monday on the view it had carried the first round against British merger partners Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan.
The chairmen of the British groups, who previously brushed aside LVMH's opposition to their merger, have agreed to meet LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault in Paris on Wednesday.

"LVMH has won the first round," a broker said. Its stock -- which has been on a seesaw ride since the luxury group began share raids on Grand Met -- was up 2.46 percent at 1,585 francs at 1105 GMT, while the bourse's CAC-40 index was 0.22 percent lower.

British newspapers say Guinness and Grand Met may propose to include Moet Hennessy, the drinks group controlled by LVMH, in UDV, the new company formed by the merger of the Guinness United Distillers and Grand Met IDV drinks businesses. In exchange, LVMH would take a stake in UDV.
The Daily Telegraph reported a three-way drinks merger, the solution proposed by Arnault all along, could generate up to 85 million pounds in additional savings.

The decision to meet in Paris follows a two-pronged attack by Arnault on the British companies. On the legal front, he is seeking the right to exercise options to buy Guinness out of the valuable joint distribution ventures they hold.
This month LVMH spent more than eight billion francs buying up Grand Met shares in an apparent aim to line up a large enough holding in the company to block the merger outright.
It is the largest single shareholder in both British groups, with 14.2 percent of Guinness and 6.37 percent of Grand Met.
